ratings_why.fun: Choosing whom to climb each turn, then watching one buff ripple down a vine, is a real drafting pull, and Bloom gives a second way to grow.
ratings_why.distinct: Copying a host's gains and blooming only when taller than the host play unlike today's six tribes, though at a glance it is still a buff-sharing tribe.

verdict_why: Cousin Dodder doesn't say what happens to its own host and climbers, which Dodder Thread now spells out; one short fix.

points.text: Cousin Dodder doesn't say whether it leaves its own host, whether its climbers copy what it steals, or whether it climbs back after the fight. Use Dodder Thread's wording.
A board's real stats depend on a hidden copy tree. Show each unit's 'copies from' and total share on hover, or the Grand Oak can't be read at a glance.
The Climb keyword is a paragraph. Keep the card line as 'Climb: copies half its host's gains', and move falling, loops and triples to the rules popup.
Lattice Ivy does nothing once Lady Hedera is out. Its golden could give its climbers twice its gains under Hedera, so it stays worth a slot.
Mistletoe Clump's 'its climbers copy what it takes' repeats Climb. Cut it so the card reads as one plain drain.

standouts.why: Dodder Thread latching onto the enemy across and drinking from it is the gatecrasher fantasy done as a rule, and the text now covers every case.
Ruin Ivy: a vine that outgrows its host and holds it up is ivy on old ruins, read in one line.
Kissing Bough pays for the whole chain at once, so you play it last onto the root; clear and satisfying.

weakest.why: Lattice Ivy is a rules tweak with no picture, and Lady Hedera makes it blank.
Hanger-on is plain gold with two conditions to check each turn; the toady fantasy is in the name only.
Barley-sugar Twiner is a stock Start of Combat buff; the twining-tightly idea doesn't show in what it does.

flags.note: Own host and own climbers during the fight aren't covered.
Full share down deep chains with Hop Bine or Viscum grows with chain depth at every level; not a loop, but big.
A third of a huge host to every falling climber can swing a fight in one death.
